requirements_to_testpoints.requirement_text:
# Binary LED

## Project Description
This is an arduino project that uses 5 LEDs to display the binary form of a number received over serial.

## Hardware Components
- Arduino Uno
- 220Ω resistor * 5
- LED * 5

## Circuit Description
Five LEDs are connected to Arduino Uno. LED 1 to 5 are connected to arduino pin2 to pin6 through 220Ω resistor, respectively. Cathode pin of each LEDs are connected to gnd2.

## Expected Behavior
When the Arduino powers up, it should:
1. Set pin2, pin3, pin4, pin5, pin6 pin mode as OUTPUT
3. Continuously read the serial monitor, which ranges from 0 to 31
4. With LED1 as the LSB and LED5 as the MSB, light up the LEDs that represent 1s in the binary form of the input number

## Success Criteria
The test is successful when:
1. When a number is entered via serial input, LEDs corresponding to the bits set to 1 in its binary representation are turned on.

## Notes for Implementation
- Serial input ranges from 0 to 31.

## Attributes
- To use 220Ω resistor, set the property name "value" to "220 ohm".

requirements_to_testpoints.stimulus: Inspect the preserved circuit and output pin configuration. Power up with io_0_valid=false. Send every integer 0 through 31 at 9600 baud, testing both newline completion and completion after 20 ms idle. Between receives, run steps with io_0_valid=false and changed io_0 values. Send malformed and out-of-range frames, then another valid integer.
requirements_to_testpoints.oracle: D2 through D6 are outputs connected respectively through 220-ohm resistors to LED1 through LED5 anodes, with cathodes at GND.2. All LEDs are initially off. Each valid receive updates the display in that control step: io_1 through io_5 equal bits 0 through 4 of the received integer, with true driving HIGH and lighting the corresponding LED. Every value 0 through 31 has its exact five-bit pattern. No receive event, malformed frames and out-of-range frames leave the previous display unchanged; the next valid frame updates it normally.
